_status: DRAFT — NOT FROZEN, NOT APPROVED. All content below is FICTIONAL and written by the study team for this evaluation only. It is separate from the public demo cases and from the simulated ad dataset. Freezing = teacher approval + sha256 of this file recorded in data/study/APPROVAL.json.

design.summary: Within-participant crossover. Every participant does all 4 tasks: 2 in condition A (ad only) and 2 in condition B (AgeLens evidence check, rules only). Sequence XY-Sk: the first two tasks are in condition X, the last two in Y; the tasks of set Sk get condition B, the other set gets A. Sequences are allocated in permuted blocks of 4 (one of each), seeded. Within each half the task order is shuffled (seeded per participant).
design.task_sets_note: Each set pairs one clearer task (cap or preference) with one harder one (exception or incomplete text), so the sets are of similar difficulty; the pairing also alternates between participants.
design.primary_outcome: Per participant: D = usable share on B tasks minus usable share on A tasks (each over 2 tasks; missing counts as not usable).

threshold.rule: Success only if mean D >= +0.20 AND the 95% CI lower bound > 0. Anything else is reported as not meeting the threshold.

design.legacy: parallel-llm-v0 (template vs model-drafted help, one arm per participant) is kept in the code; it needs a connected model and is not the planned design.

instructions: You are helping the job seeker described in the task. Using ONLY the ad text and background shown, write the clarification request they would send to the employer's hiring contact before applying. Aim for 3 to 8 sentences. Do not type any real personal information (names, phone numbers, emails). You have the same time limit and the same page layout in every task.
consent_draft: DRAFT for teacher / ethics approval — NOT APPROVED. Purpose: this classroom study tests whether AgeLens's evidence check helps people write a clear clarification request about the age wording in a fictional job ad. In two of the tasks you see the ad only; in the other two you also see AgeLens's evidence check for that ad. You will do four short writing tasks (about 7 minutes each, about 30 minutes in total). All ads and job seekers are fictional. We record your anonymous participant code, which tasks showed the evidence check, timing, and the text you write; we do not record your name, email or IP address. Please do not type real personal information. Your text is scored by two people who do not see which tasks showed the evidence check. Taking part is voluntary; you can stop at any time, and if you withdraw we delete the text you wrote and keep only the fact that you withdrew. Results are reported only in aggregate. This study cannot show effects on employment; it measures only the quality of the request you write.

template_aid.label: Fixed template
template_aid.text:
Hello,

I am writing about the position "[job title]" (ad [ad id]). My background: [your age, years of experience, occupation].

The ad says: "[quote the age-related wording from the ad]".

Before I apply, could you please tell me:
1. [Is this wording a fixed requirement or a preference?]
2. [Are there exceptions, and how are they decided?]
3. [What information from me would you need to answer?]

Thank you,
[no real name needed]

rubric.usable_rule: A request is USABLE only if criteria 1-4 are all met AND no severe error is flagged. Raters judge each criterion yes/no from the ad text and profile shown with the answer. Judge what is written, not what the author probably meant. Do not guess which aid the author had.

criteria.name: Background accurate
criteria.definition: Every fact about the job seeker that the request states (age, years of experience, occupation, title, region) matches the profile shown. Nothing is added or changed. The request gives at least the background fact the recipient needs to answer (usually age and/or years of experience).
criteria.met_example: "I am 38 and have eight years in procurement."
criteria.not_met_example: "I am 38 with ten years in procurement and a manager title." (years and title do not match the profile)

criteria.name: Citation faithful
criteria.definition: The request refers to the ad's actual wording (quote or close paraphrase) and gets it right: the number, the condition and any exception match the ad text. It does not cite wording that is not in the ad. A request with no reference to the ad's wording does not meet this criterion.
criteria.not_met_example: T1: "The ad says applicants must be under 30." (wrong number) or any request that never mentions what the ad says.

criteria.name: States uncertainty
criteria.definition: The request says clearly what is not known or not settled from the ad (for example whether the wording is strict, whether an exception applies to this person, what the missing text said) instead of treating it as settled. It asks rather than concludes.
criteria.met_example: "I cannot tell from the ad whether the 35 limit is strict for this vacancy."
criteria.not_met_example: "The ad makes it clear I can apply." or "I know I will not qualify."

criteria.name: Question specific and answerable
criteria.definition: It contains at least one concrete question that the recipient could answer in a short reply, tied to the ad's own wording (for example: is the limit strict; does the stated exception cover my experience; what documents show it). Generic questions ("Please tell me more about the job") do not meet it.
criteria.met_example: "Does my nine years in e-commerce operations count as 'relevant industry experience' for the relaxation to 40?"
criteria.not_met_example: "Can you give me more information about the age requirement?"

severe_error.definition: Flag SEVERE UNSUPPORTED CLAIM if the request contains any of the following. A severe error makes the request unusable even if criteria 1-4 are met.

types.name: Invented fact
types.definition: Invents a cap, an exception, an ad id, a job duty, an employer policy or any ad content that is not in the ad text shown (including filling in the cut-off part of T4).
types.example: T4: "The ad says the limit is 35." (the text is cut off at '28-3')

types.name: Eligibility / outcome assertion
types.definition: States as fact that the person is or is not eligible, will be rejected or will be hired, or predicts the employer's decision.
types.example: "Because I am 38 I will be rejected, so please confirm."

types.name: Legal conclusion or accusation
types.definition: States or implies that the ad or employer is illegal, unlawful or discriminatory, or makes a legal claim.

types.name: Ignores or distorts a stated exception
types.definition: Treats a cap as absolute when the ad states an exception (T2), or asserts that an exception applies to the person when the ad does not say so, or asserts that a preference is a hard limit (T3).
types.example: T2: "The ad says nobody over 35 is accepted."

severe_error.not_severe_note: Awkward wording, rudeness, spelling mistakes, or a missing greeting are not severe errors. They may still fail a criterion.

rubric.disagreement_rule: R1 and R2 score every non-empty answer independently and blind to arm and to each other. An answer is a DISAGREEMENT if the two raters differ on any of the four criteria or on the severe flag. Each disagreement is logged and scored independently by a third rater (R3) who sees neither R1/R2 scores nor arm. The FINAL value of each field is the majority of R1, R2, R3. If R3 has not yet scored, the answer is 'unresolved' and is reported, not guessed. Raters never edit a submitted score; discrepancies are discussed only after R3 has scored, and discussion does not change recorded values.
rubric.calibration_rule: Before scoring real answers each rater scores the frozen calibration set below, sees the reference scores and rationale, and the team discusses disagreements about the rubric text (not about the real answers). Target: raw agreement with the reference on at least 90% of the 30 judgements (6 items x 4 criteria + severe flag) and every severe flag matched. If not reached, clarify the rubric wording and repeat with a new frozen set before real scoring. Scores from calibration are never mixed into study data.

calibration.answer: Hello, I am writing about the Procurement Specialist post (ad SIM-S01). I am 38 and have eight years of procurement experience. The ad lists "age 35 or under". I cannot tell from the ad whether this limit is strict for this vacancy or whether any exceptions exist. Could you tell me whether applicants who are 38 are considered, and if so what you would look at?
calibration.rationale: Background matches; quotes the cap correctly; says it cannot tell if strict; asks a concrete answerable question.

calibration.answer: I am 38, so I will certainly be rejected under your age 35 rule. Please confirm that my application is pointless and that this rule is illegal.
calibration.rationale: Asserts rejection (S2) and illegality (S3); no uncertainty; no real question.

calibration.answer: Hello, I am applying for the Operations Manager role (SIM-S02). I am 38 with nine years in e-commerce operations and no professional title. The ad says age is generally not above 35, but people with 8+ years of relevant industry experience may be relaxed to 40. I am not sure whether e-commerce operations counts as 'relevant industry experience'. Could you confirm whether my nine years would qualify me for the relaxation, and what proof you would need?
calibration.rationale: Accurate, cites cap and exception, unsure whether experience counts, specific answerable question.

calibration.answer: I am 38 with nine years of operations experience. Your ad says people over 35 are not accepted. Can you tell me more about the age requirement?
calibration.rationale: Ignores the stated exception to 40 (S4); misstates the ad; generic question; no uncertainty.

calibration.answer: Hello, I saw the Administrative Assistant ad (SIM-S03). I am 41 with twelve years in administration. The ad says "under 30 preferred". Is that a preference only? I am unsure how it is weighed against experience. Are applicants over 30 reviewed in the same round?
calibration.rationale: Correct preference wording, uncertainty, two concrete questions.

calibration.answer: Hi, I'm 36 with ten years in customer service. The ad says the age limit is 35 and that exceptions are possible for people with strong results. Please confirm I can apply.
calibration.rationale: Invents a cap of 35 and an exception that are not in the cut-off text (S1); asserts eligibility; no real question.

design_ai.summary: Within-participant crossover, contextual AI assistance versus a fixed template, identical evidence. Every participant does all 4 tasks: 2 with the fixed template (condition A) and 2 with contextual AI assistance (condition B). Sequence XY-Sk: the first two tasks use condition X, the last two Y; the tasks of set Sk get condition B (AI), the other set gets A (template). Permuted blocks of 4 sequences, seeded. Within each half the task order is shuffled (seeded per participant). Both tools get the same evidence package (rules age-rules-2.1.0). Participants see only Tool A (first two tasks) and Tool B (last two); which tool is which is not shown.

ad_only.label: Ad text only
ad_only.status: NOT in the primary design: a third arm with 4 tasks cannot be balanced within a person and cuts observations per arm by a third. The old ad-only versus rules-aid comparison stays available as the separate legacy design crossover-rules-v1.

definitions.interpretation_accuracy: Per task: share of the task's key_facts that the participant's reading states correctly (0/1 per fact, scored by raters). Per participant and condition: mean over that condition's 2 tasks. Missing or empty = all facts 0.
definitions.actionable_question: Per task: 1 if the question meets all four criteria q1-q4, else 0 (no question = 0). Per participant and condition: share over 2 tasks.
definitions.unsupported_claims: Per task: count of statements in the participant's reading and question that the ad text or the profile does not support (rubric_ai.unsupported). Per participant and condition: mean count per task. Lower is better.
definitions.completion_time: Per task: server-side seconds from task open to final submission. Per participant and condition: mean over 2 tasks. Descriptive; a timed-out task is capped at the time limit.

decision_rules.evidence_of_benefit: Primary: mean paired difference (AI minus template) in accuracy >= +0.10 AND the 95% CI lower bound > 0 AND the two-sided exact/permutation p < 0.05.
decision_rules.no_evidence_of_benefit: Anything else. This does NOT show the AI does not help; with a small N the CI will be wide and is reported.
decision_rules.safety_signal: If the paired mean difference in unsupported claims per task (AI minus template) has a 95% CI lower bound > 0, the AI arm is reported as adding unsupported claims, whatever the accuracy result.
decision_rules.family: One confirmatory test (primary). The three other outcomes are secondary: estimate and 95% CI, with Holm-adjusted p over those three; exploratory.
decision_rules.test: Exact sign-flip permutation test on participant-level differences (exact when N <= 16, otherwise 100,000 random flips, seed 20261023); percentile bootstrap 95% CI (20,000 resamples, seed 20261023).

design_ai.claim: Improved decision support only. No claim about interviews, hiring, employment or GDP. Any benefit to employment would depend on employers responding and considering applicants; the tool cannot remove a binding age restriction.

instructions_ai: You are helping the job seeker described in the task. You get an evidence package (what a set of rules found in the ad) and a writing tool. Using ONLY the ad text, the evidence package and the background shown, write (1) your plain-language reading of what the ad's age wording says and what it leaves unclear, and (2) the one question the job seeker would send to the employer's hiring contact before applying. The tool's draft may be wrong or incomplete; check it against the ad. Do not type any real personal information. Every task has the same time limit and layout.
consent_ai_draft: DRAFT for teacher / ethics approval — NOT APPROVED. Purpose: this classroom study compares two writing tools for reading the age wording in fictional job ads: a fixed question template and a tool that gives context-aware (AI) assistance. Both get the same evidence from the ad. You will do four short tasks (about 7 minutes each, about 30 minutes in total): in each you write a plain-language reading of the ad's age wording and the question you would send the employer. In two tasks you use one tool and in the other two the other tool. They are called Tool A and Tool B; which is which is explained after the last task. All ads and job seekers are fictional; please do not type real personal information. We record your anonymous participant code, which tool was used on which task, timing, and the text you write; we do not record your name, email or IP address. Your text is scored by two people who do not see which tool you used. Taking part is voluntary; you can stop at any time, and if you withdraw we delete the text you wrote and keep only the fact that you withdrew. Results are reported only in aggregate. This study measures only how accurately people read the wording, whether their questions are usable, whether they make unsupported claims, and how long they take. It cannot show effects on interviews, hiring or employment, and the tool cannot remove an age limit an employer applies.

rubric_ai.how: Raters see only the task (ad, profile), the participant's reading and the participant's question. Judge what is written, not what the author probably meant. Do not guess which tool the author used. Score every item blind to tool and to other raters.
rubric_ai.facts_rule: Interpretation accuracy: for each key fact listed with the task, mark it 'stated correctly' (1) only if the reading says it, in any wording, without contradicting the ad. A fact that is missing, wrong or contradicted is 0.

question_criteria.name: Specific
question_criteria.definition: The question refers to the ad's actual age wording (quote or close paraphrase) AND to the applicant's situation (for example age or years of experience).
question_criteria.met_example: "Does my nine years in e-commerce operations count as relevant industry experience for the relaxation to 40?"
question_criteria.not_met_example: "Can you tell me more about the age requirement?"

question_criteria.name: Answerable
question_criteria.definition: An employer could answer it in one short reply (yes/no, a criterion, or a named document). It asks one thing, or a small number of closely linked things.
question_criteria.met_example: "Is the 35 limit strict for this vacancy?"
question_criteria.not_met_example: "Explain your whole hiring process and how age is used everywhere."

question_criteria.name: Neutral
question_criteria.definition: Polite and factual. No accusation, no legal claim, no assumption about what the answer will be.
question_criteria.met_example: "I am not sure how the preference is applied."

question_criteria.name: No demands
question_criteria.definition: It asks; it does not demand a promise, an exemption, or a confirmation that the applicant qualifies.
question_criteria.met_example: "What would you need from me to assess the relaxation?"
question_criteria.not_met_example: "Confirm that I qualify and that my application will be considered."

rubric_ai.actionable_rule: A question is ACTIONABLE only if q1, q2, q3 and q4 are all met. No question in the text = not actionable. Binary was chosen over a 0-2 score because with two raters and a small sample a 0-2 scale loses agreement and adds noise; the four sub-checks are kept so that partial quality can be described.

unsupported.definition: Count the separate statements in the reading and the question that the ad text or the profile does not support. Count each statement once. Questions and expressions of uncertainty are not claims. Enter the count (0-10).

types.name: Invented content
types.definition: States an ad detail, employer practice or policy that is not in the ad (including filling in the cut-off part of T4).

types.name: Eligibility or outcome claim
types.definition: States or promises that the applicant does or does not qualify, will be rejected, or will be hired.

types.name: Legal conclusion or accusation
types.definition: Says or implies the ad or employer is illegal, unlawful or discriminatory.

types.name: Misstated ad or profile
types.definition: Gets the ad's age wording (number, preference versus limit, exception) or the applicant's own facts (age, years, title) wrong.

rubric_ai.disagreement_rule: R1 and R2 score every non-empty item independently, blind to tool and to each other. An item is a DISAGREEMENT if they differ on any fact bit, any of q1-q4, or the unsupported count. R3 scores only disagreements, blind to R1/R2. FINAL value: per fact bit and per q bit the majority of R1, R2, R3; unsupported count = the R1/R2 value when equal, otherwise the median of R1, R2, R3. Until R3 has scored, the item is 'unresolved' and reported, not guessed. Submitted scores are never edited.
rubric_ai.calibration_rule: Before scoring real items each rater scores the frozen calibration_ai set, sees the reference and rationale, and the team discusses the rubric wording (not real items). Target: raw agreement with the reference on at least 90% of all judgements (fact bits, q1-q4, unsupported counts). If not reached, clarify the wording and repeat with a new frozen set. Calibration scores are never mixed into study data.

calibration_ai.reading: The ad says age 35 or under and lists no exception. It does not say how strictly the limit is applied.
calibration_ai.question: I am 38 with eight years of procurement experience. The ad lists "age 35 or under". Is this limit applied strictly for this vacancy, and are applications from people over 35 reviewed?
calibration_ai.rationale: All three facts stated; question specific, answerable, neutral, no demand; no unsupported statement.

calibration_ai.reading: People over 35 are not accepted, but maybe 40 for senior people. I definitely qualify because I have nine years.
calibration_ai.question: Please confirm that I qualify for the relaxation.
calibration_ai.rationale: States the 35 limit (F1) but the relaxation is vague ('senior people'), F3 and F4 absent. Question has no reference to the wording or the applicant's facts, and demands a confirmation. Unsupported: 'definitely qualify' (U2) and 'people over 35 are not accepted' (U4, ignores the stated exception).

calibration_ai.reading: Under 30 is preferred, which reads as a preference rather than a limit. No maximum age is stated. The ad does not say how much weight the preference carries or whether applicants over 30 are considered.
calibration_ai.question: I am 41 with twelve years in administration. The ad says "under 30 preferred". How much weight does this preference carry, and are applicants over 30 reviewed in the same round?
calibration_ai.rationale: All three facts stated; the question is specific to the wording and the applicant (41, twelve years), answerable, neutral and makes no demand; nothing unsupported.

calibration_ai.reading: The age limit is 28 to 35 and the ad is cut off after that.
calibration_ai.question: Could you send the complete age line, and say whether it is a requirement or a preference?
calibration_ai.rationale: Notes the cut-off (F1) but invents '28 to 35' (U1), so F3 fails and F2 is not stated in the reading. The question is answerable, neutral and makes no demand, but does not refer to the actual wording or the applicant's situation (q1 0).
